description:
FILED s543 by the reviewing session (2026-11-24), found while widening #5310's probe list.  PRE-EXISTING and old: MAIN-READY-102, -106, main cbcc9165 and s543k's tree 3b20d5ab all answer the same.  Probe files with perl's answers: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/review/probes-1124/ (h2.pl, i.pl, k.pl; *.perl = perl 5.40.3, *.main = main).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl on main cbcc9165):
    print "k5 ", eval(q{package T; our $w = 1; sub n4 { my $w = 4; $w + 1 } n4() . " $w"}), "\n";
    print "i1 ", eval(q{package Q; our $w = 1; my $w = 4; $w + 1}), "\n";
    # perl: k5 5 1 / i1 5
    # PCL:  k5 2 1 / i1 2          (the lexical's reads are the `our` variable's)

WRONG ON MAIN (each perl 5, PCL 2 unless noted):
  the reproducer's two rows; `sub n { my ($w) = @_; $w + 1 } n(4)`; `my $w = shift` / `my $w = $_[0]`; a signature `sub n ($w) { $w + 1 }`; `my ($w, $k) = @_` (perl 9, PCL 6: only the clashing name is wrong); a bare block `{ my ($w) = (4); $w + 1 }`; an anonymous sub `my $f = sub { my $w = 4; $w + 1 }`; `for my $w (4) { return $w + 1 }`; a closure over the inner lexical (`my $c = sub { $w + 1 }`); a hash `our %w = (k => 1); sub n { my %w = (k => 4); $w{k} + 1 }` (PCL 1); `$w .= "x"; $w` on the inner lexical (perl 4x, PCL 1); and `use vars '$u'; $u = 1; sub n { my $u = 4; $u + 1 }` (the same answer with no `our` in the text).
  A second face, not reduced: `eval q{package T; { package U; our $w = 1; sub n9 { my $w = 4; $w + 1 } n9() . " $w" }}` returns undef (perl "5 1") -- print $@ first.

RIGHT ON MAIN (the bounds): the same text at FILE level in all three package forms (`{ package Q; ... }`, `package Q;` statement, the reproducer's sub); the eval WITHOUT the leading `package` (`eval q{our $w = 1; sub n { my $w = 4; $w + 1 } n()}`); a plain global instead of an `our` (`package T; $z = 1; sub n { my $z = 4; $z + 1 }`, `$T::q = 1`); an ARRAY (`our @w = (1); sub n { my @w = @_; "@w" }`); a signature on an ANONYMOUS sub (`my $f = sub ($z) { $z + 1 }`); and -- unexplained -- `sub n3 { my $w = 4; $w++; $w } n3() . " $w $Q::w"` (5 1 1 as perl).

So: a leading `package` REGION in an eval text + a name the text declares `our` (or `use vars`) + a later `my` of that name -- the lexical's uses take the package variable's spelling.  The file-level block requalifier asks the same binder and is right, so the suspect is what differs for an eval text: `Parser2::_requalify_eval_text` / `_requalify_region` with the region's `$keep`, or `Binder::requalify_home`'s answer for a token under a `my` that follows an `our` record the TEXT declares (s543k's `Binder::text_declares` is the neighbour; it did not change this).

THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken: the reviewing session files, the member measures): for the reproducer's k5 text print `Binder::requalify_home($tok, '$w')` at the `$w` token inside the sub body -- (undef, lexical) means the binder is right and the rewrite happens elsewhere (then diff the eval text's emission for `$w` inside `n4` against the file-level program's); ('T', our) means the binder homes a lexical use to the earlier `our` in an eval text.  Also explain why the `$w++` row is right: it bounds the mechanism.

BAR: every WRONG row above = perl, every RIGHT row unchanged; a guard row in `Pl/t/eval-capture-01.t`; name resolution: the sweep is the gate.
subject: SILENT WRONG: in an eval text behind a leading `package T;`, a `my $w` declared AFTER the text's own `our $w` (same scope, a named sub, an anonymous sub, a `for my`) reads the PACKAGE variable -- `eval q{package T; our $w = 1; sub n { my $w = 4; $w + 1 } n()}` gives 2 (perl 5)
triage_reason: a silent wrong of name resolution in a string eval (eval STRING must work): a `my` reads the text's own `our` of the same name behind a `package` statement; IN
